method: parse the ggml logical decode graph; collapse view/reshape/permute no-op tensors into their single producer; compute the longest real-op chain. Structural (unweighted by kernel duration); weighted path is a separate follow-up.

structural_critical_path.per_layer_cycle: rmsnorm -> mul -> mmq(Q) -> rmsnorm -> mul -> rope -> flash -> mmq(O) -> add -> rmsnorm -> mul -> mmq(gate) -> glu -> mmq(down) -> add
structural_critical_path.finding: llama carries 4 of 7 matmuls per layer on the structural critical path: Q, O, gate, down. The K and V projections are off-path (parallel with Q's norm+rope branch), and the two set_rows KV-cache writes hang off the K/V branches, not the Q chain.

note: Structural dependency fact, not a wall claim. Follow-up trace (nv-tinygrad-critical-path-trace-20260819.json) shows tinygrad ALREADY carries only Q/O/gate/down on its critical path, so reproducing llama's matmul spine is not the lever. The open lever is the support glue between those matmuls.
